title: Mockup Updates — v1.4
subtitle: The thirty comments on the 18 August deck, screen by screen: what the mockup looked like when the comments were written, and what it looks like now.
blurb: Each screen is shown before and after, with the comments it answered underneath. A dashed frame on the right means the screen was deleted by this round.

screens.name: Create your account
notes: Slide 1
"Your name" added at the top of the form, and "Create a password" after the email address — both moved here from A7, which this round deletes. An account is one form now.
Slide 1
The mobile hint reads "OTP verification required." and the email hint "Farm reports are sent to this email address." — what the address is for, rather than what it is not.
Slide 1
The gap between "I agree to the Terms of Use and" and "Privacy Policy" is closed. The links keep their full tap target; the padding just stops taking up room in the line.
Slide 1
The paragraph about signing in afterwards with either identifier is deleted.
Slide 1
The button reads "Send OTP to mobile number", and waits for all five answers: name, number, address, password, tick.

screens.name: Verify code
notes: Slide 2
The heading and the sentence beneath it are one line: "Enter OTP sent to +966 5X XXX XXXX".
Slide 2

Four digits, not six. It deviates from WF4.038 and the README says why: a code that dies in ten minutes and locks the account after five wrong tries does not need two more digits, and two fewer are two fewer to carry between apps.

screens.name: Your details and units
notes: Slide 3
Deleted. The name and the password are part of creating an account and are asked on A5; the land unit is not an account fact at all and is asked on A9, one screen before the app first prints an area.
Slide 3
Password recovery used to borrow this screen for its last step, so a returning user was asked for his name again on the way to a new password. Reset is now three steps of its own.

screens.name: Add your farm
notes: Slide 4
"How do you measure land?" arrives here, pre-selected from the country (WF4.043).
Slide 4
The lead loses "— pick whichever suits your farm".
Slide 4
The survey card now says what the satellite does — detects cultivated plots and trees from the boundary — and that plots can be added or deleted after the survey.
Slide 4

Both cards end in "Choose this option". The card is no longer itself the tap target, and B12's copy of this fork was replaced by the same component, so the second farm cannot be described in different words from the first.

screens.name: What should our satellite survey?
notes: Slide 5
The title asks about the satellite. Each option says how it is priced — per area for field crops, per tree for the trees — because that is the half of the choice the farmer is actually making.
Slide 5
"Name your farm" moves to the top, above the options, and loses the note about being numbered automatically: the placeholder already shows the name he gets if he types nothing.
Slide 5
That placeholder reads Farm 1. It counts the farms the account holds, which during registration is none, whatever the demo database is carrying.

screens.name: Draw my own plots
notes: Slide 6
The bar reads "Farm 1 · Plot 1" over "Trace your plot boundary".
Slide 6
The area is labelled "Plot area" and says that it follows the shape being dragged. It always did; nothing on the screen said so.
Slide 6
"Name this plot", and the placeholder is "Plot 1". P1 is gone from the whole app — drawn plots, survey results and the 32 plots in the fixtures — so no screen shows both conventions.
Slide 6
The search bar opens three ways in: search on the map, enter a town or locality, use my current location. Nobody knows their coordinates.

screens.name: Survey my whole farm
notes: Slide 7
The bar reads the farm name over "Trace your farm boundary", and the area is labelled "Farm area".
Slide 7
The farm boundary is blue, against the green of a plot. Brown was the other suggestion; the basemap is tan desert soil, and a brown line over it is a line nobody can see.
Slide 7

"Draw your farm boundary to cover open fields and tree areas. No need to include greenhouses, warehouses or other structures." This reverses the old instruction to include buildings — the farmer now draws what he is buying.
Slide 7
The same three ways to find the land.

screens.name: Reset your password
notes: Slide 3
Three steps of its own now that A7 is gone: identifier, code, new password.

screens.name: Add a farm
notes: Slide 4
Draws A9's fork rather than its own copy of it, so both carry the new wording and the "Choose this option" buttons.

screens.name: Plots
notes: Slide 6
Every plot reads "Plot 1" rather than "P1", here and in every list that crosses farms.

screens.name: Find your land
notes: Slides 6, 7
New. The three ways anyone actually finds their land, behind the search bar on both drawing screens.
